turns: Which NVIDIA products were hit by the new US export license requirements for China in fiscal 2023?
reference_answer: The US government imposed new license requirements on exports to China (including Hong Kong and Macau) and Russia that cover NVIDIA's A100 and H100 integrated circuits, DGX or other systems and boards that use them, and the A100X, plus any future NVIDIA chip above certain performance and chip-to-chip I/O thresholds.

turns: What supply chain risks did NVIDIA cite in fiscal 2023?
reference_answer: NVIDIA uses third parties to manufacture and assemble its products, faces long manufacturing lead times, and has no guaranteed wafer, component and capacity supply. It placed non-cancellable orders well ahead of historical lead times, and its growing purchase obligations and prepaids could lead to inventory write-downs, cancellation penalties and impairments if its demand estimates are wrong.

turns: What charge did NVIDIA record after the US required a license for H20 exports to China?
reference_answer: On April 9, 2025 the US government told NVIDIA that exports of H20 products to China require a license. NVIDIA recorded a $4.5 billion charge in the first quarter of fiscal 2026 for H20 excess inventory and purchase obligations, less than first expected because it could reuse some materials.

turns: Why did NVIDIA's planned purchase of a chip IP company from SoftBank fall through, and what will it cost?
reference_answer: In February 2022 NVIDIA and SoftBank terminated the agreement for NVIDIA to buy Arm because of significant regulatory challenges. NVIDIA expected a $1.36 billion charge in the first quarter of fiscal 2023 to write off the prepayment made at signing in September 2020.

turns: How did crypto mining affect NVIDIA's gaming business in fiscal 2019?
reference_answer: NVIDIA said demand for desktop gaming GPUs used for cryptocurrency mining, and its after-effects, distorted Gaming revenue trends in fiscal 2019. Revenue from cryptocurrency-specific products was $306 million, against $273 million in fiscal 2018, and NVIDIA expected it to be negligible going forward.

turns: How much did Mellanox contribute to NVIDIA's revenue in fiscal 2021?
reference_answer: Data Center revenue grew 124% in fiscal 2021, driven by the Mellanox acquisition and the ramp of the Ampere architecture. Mellanox contributed 10% of total company revenue.

turns: How do US export controls on China affect NVIDIA's and AMD's data center GPUs?
reference_answer: NVIDIA needs licenses to export A100 and H100 chips and systems that use them to China and Russia. AMD cannot ship its Instinct MI250, MI300X, MI300A and MI388X accelerators (or certain Versal FPGAs) to China, or to customers whose ultimate parent is in a D5 country, without a license.

turns: What did China's cybersecurity regulator decide about Micron's products, and what does it mean for Micron?
reference_answer: China's Cyberspace Administration (CAC) opened a cybersecurity review of Micron products sold in China on March 31, 2023, and on May 21, 2023 concluded they presented a cybersecurity risk, so critical information infrastructure operators in China cannot buy Micron products. No list of those operators is published, so the impact on Micron's business is uncertain.

turns: How much did Micron write down its inventory in fiscal 2023 and why?
reference_answer: Because of the weak pricing environment, with lower average selling prices for DRAM and NAND, Micron recognized $1.83 billion of charges in 2023 to write inventories down to their estimated net realizable value. Its gross margin fell to negative 9% from 45% in 2022.

turns: How did HBM and AI demand affect Micron's results in fiscal 2025?
reference_answer: Micron shifted part of its DRAM supply to data center and hyperscale cloud customers to meet AI-driven demand, with an emphasis on HBM. The richer mix, higher average selling prices and lower costs raised its consolidated gross margin to 40% in 2025 from 22% in 2024.

turns: Which chipmakers discussed the US investigation into semiconductor imports that could lead to tariffs?
reference_answer: KLA and Micron discussed the investigations that the US opened in April 2025 under Section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962 into the national security effects of semiconductor imports. The scope covers semiconductors, manufacturing equipment and derivative products such as substrates and bare wafers, and the results were unknown.

turns: What government inquiry about China shipments did Applied Materials disclose?
reference_answer: In August 2022 Applied received a subpoena from the U.S. Attorney's Office for the District of Massachusetts requesting information about certain shipments to China customers. Applied said it was cooperating fully and could not predict the outcome.

turns: How did the coronavirus outbreak affect Applied Materials' operations in early 2020?
reference_answer: Applied said the COVID-19 outbreak in China had affected and could further affect its operations, customers and suppliers through quarantines, facility closures, and travel and logistics restrictions. It did not expect a material impact on fiscal 2020 results, but expected the timing of revenue within the year to change.

turns: How do the October 2022 BIS rules affect KLA's business in China?
reference_answer: The BIS Rules published in October 2022 restrict semiconductor, semiconductor manufacturing, supercomputer and advanced computing items and end uses, limiting KLA's ability to sell, ship and support certain equipment for counterparties, mainly China-based companies in advanced semiconductor manufacturing. They also restrict US persons' activities, on top of earlier controls that added many entities to the Entity List.

turns: Which chipmaking equipment needs an export license for Chinese customers under the new rules from late 2022?
reference_answer: KLA said the New BIS Rules issued in October 2022 impose export license requirements on effectively all KLA products and services for customers in China that fabricate non-planar ICs (such as FinFET or GAAFET) or logic ICs at 14/16nm and below. KLA was applying for licenses and assessing the impact, which could reduce its remaining performance obligations or require returning customer deposits.

turns: Why did Lam Research's business slow in fiscal 2023?
reference_answer: Wafer fabrication equipment spending fell, mainly because of demand weakness in memory, and US restrictions on sales of equipment, parts and service to certain customers in China further hurt demand. Supply constraints in the first half eased, and Lam shipped nearly all backlogged systems in the second half, then started a restructuring plan to fit the lower business levels.

turns: How much CHIPS Act support does Texas Instruments expect, and for which fabs?
reference_answer: TI expects $7.5 billion to $9.5 billion from the CHIPS Act through 2034, including the investment tax credit and up to $1.6 billion of direct funding for its three 300mm wafer fabs under construction in Sherman, Texas and Lehi, Utah. It received $588 million of cash benefit from qualifying capital expenditures in 2024.

turns: What did Texas Instruments say about the CHIPS Act when it passed in 2022?
reference_answer: The CHIPS and Science Act, enacted in August 2022, funds manufacturing grants and research and creates a 25% investment tax credit for US semiconductor manufacturing investments. TI was evaluating the benefit and expected cash benefits from the credit on qualifying US capital expenditures.

turns: What did Intel's 2024 Restructuring Plan involve?
reference_answer: The plan reduces headcount (about 15% of the core Intel workforce by early 2025), consolidates real estate, reviews the business portfolio, rationalizes capital investments and cuts operating expenses. Intel recognized $2.8 billion of restructuring charges in 2024.

turns: What risks come with Intel's plan to expand its own manufacturing and become a foundry?
reference_answer: Intel's large capacity investments under its IDM 2.0 strategy heighten underutilization risk, meaning higher costs, shorter useful lives and accelerated depreciation if demand falls short. Its growing R&D investments may take years to contribute to results, or never do.

turns: What deal did Intel sign for its Altera business in 2025?
reference_answer: On April 14, 2025 Intel agreed to sell 51% of Altera's common stock to an affiliate of Silver Lake Partners, with closing expected in the second half of 2025. After closing Intel expected to deconsolidate Altera.

turns: What happened when Intel took Mobileye public?
reference_answer: Intel completed Mobileye's IPO on October 26, 2022, covering about 6% of Mobileye's capital stock. The shares trade on Nasdaq as MBLY, Intel received about $1.0 billion of net proceeds, and it kept 94% of Mobileye.

turns: Why might Intel come to depend on TSMC to make its products?
reference_answer: Intel has not secured any significant external foundry customer. Without one for Intel 14A it may pause or stop developing that node, and products needing nodes beyond Intel 18A and 18A-P would then be made by third-party foundries, particularly TSMC, with which Intel has no long-term contract.

turns: Which AMD products need a license to ship to China under the US export controls?
reference_answer: Controls on ECCN 3A090 and 4A090 items prevent AMD from shipping its Instinct MI250, MI300X, MI300A and MI388X and its Versal VC2802 and VE2802 FPGAs to China, or to customers whose ultimate parent is in a D5 country, without a license. AMD must also file a Notified Advanced Computing (NAC) notification with BIS 25 days before shipping certain products.

turns: How did buying an FPGA maker change AMD's business in 2022?
reference_answer: AMD completed its acquisition of Xilinx in February 2022, adding adaptable hardware platforms such as FPGAs and a presence in embedded markets. Embedded segment revenue rose to $4.6 billion from $246 million in 2021, and its operating income to $2.3 billion.

turns: What did AMD say about its planned acquisition of ZT Systems?
reference_answer: In August 2024 AMD agreed to acquire ZT Systems, with closing expected in the first half of 2025 subject to regulatory approvals and other conditions. AMD warned that, as with other deals such as Silo AI, the benefits depend on integrating the acquired business successfully.

turns: What did Broadcom pay for VMware?
reference_answer: Broadcom completed the VMware acquisition on November 22, 2023 for about $30.8 billion in cash and 544 million Broadcom shares (split-adjusted) with a fair value of $53.4 billion.

turns: Which security software business did Broadcom buy in late 2019, and how did it pay for it?
reference_answer: On November 4, 2019 Broadcom bought Symantec's Enterprise Security business for about $10.7 billion in cash, funded through a credit agreement providing up to $12 billion in term loans.

turns: How did the Huawei settlement affect Qualcomm's fiscal 2020 licensing revenue?
reference_answer: In July 2020 Qualcomm settled its dispute with Huawei over the license that expired at the end of 2019 and signed a new long-term global patent license agreement. It recorded $1.8 billion of licensing revenue from Huawei in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2020 for amounts due under the settlement and royalties for the March and June 2020 quarters.

turns: What risk does Qualcomm face from its biggest phone customer building its own chips?
reference_answer: Apple bought Intel's modem assets in December 2019 and is developing its own modems, so Qualcomm expects Apple to use its own modem products instead of Qualcomm's. Apple has also used a competitor's modems, and its purchases of Qualcomm's thin modem products carry lower revenue and margins than integrated modem and application processor products.

turns: How much did Amazon lose on its Rivian investment in 2022?
reference_answer: Amazon's other income (expense) included a valuation loss of $12.7 billion in 2022 on its equity investment in Rivian, after an $11.8 billion gain in 2021.

turns: Why did Procter & Gamble's operating income fall in fiscal 2019?
reference_answer: Operating income fell $7.9 billion (59%), mainly because of $8.3 billion of non-cash impairment charges on Shave Care goodwill and Gillette intangible assets, partly offset by higher net sales.

turns: What charge did Exxon record when it pulled out of Russia in 2022?
reference_answer: After Russia's invasion of Ukraine, Exxon decided to discontinue operations on the Sakhalin-1 project and exit the venture, and its first-quarter 2022 results included $3.4 billion of after-tax charges, mostly the impairment of its Sakhalin operations.

turns: What did the Change Healthcare cyberattack cost UnitedHealth in 2024?
reference_answer: UnitedHealth incurred $2.2 billion of direct response costs in 2024, including the cost of interest-free loans to care providers (more than $9 billion lent), higher medical care spending, network restoration and notifying affected people.

turns: What did NextEra's Florida utility spend restoring power after the 2022 hurricanes?
reference_answer: Hurricanes Ian and Nicole hit FPL's service area in 2022, and FPL incurred about $1.3 billion of recoverable storm restoration costs, which it petitioned the Florida PSC to recover in January 2023.

turns: What did the FDIC special assessment cost Bank of America in 2023?
reference_answer: The FDIC imposed a special assessment to recover the Deposit Insurance Fund's losses from the closure of Silicon Valley Bank and Signature Bank, and Bank of America recorded $2.1 billion of noninterest expense for it in the fourth quarter of 2023.

turns: How much did Caterpillar expect tariffs to cost it in 2025?
reference_answer: Caterpillar expected the incremental tariff impact for 2025 to be about $1.3 billion to $1.5 billion, net of some mitigating actions and cost controls, with the impact larger in the fourth quarter than the third.

turns: When did Exxon close its acquisition of Pioneer?
reference_answer: Exxon's acquisition of Pioneer Natural Resources closed on May 3, 2024.

turns: Which company's health care technology business was hit by a cyberattack in 2024?
reference_answer: UnitedHealth Group: its recently acquired Change Healthcare business was hit by a cyberattack in 2024 involving protected health information and personally identifiable information.

turns: What did a court rule about Google's search business in 2024?
reference_answer: In August 2024 the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia ruled that Google violated antitrust laws relating to Search and Search advertising, in the case brought by the DOJ and state Attorneys General. A separate proceeding would decide remedies, which could include structural remedies.

turns: Which company wrote down the value of a razor brand, and by how much?
reference_answer: Procter & Gamble recorded $8.3 billion of non-cash impairment charges in fiscal 2019 on Shave Care goodwill and Gillette indefinite-lived intangible assets.

turns: Which companies paid a special FDIC charge after the 2023 bank failures?
reference_answer: Bank of America recorded a $2.1 billion FDIC special assessment in the fourth quarter of 2023, imposed to recover the Deposit Insurance Fund's losses from the closure of Silicon Valley Bank and Signature Bank.

turns: Which company left an oil and gas project in Russia after the invasion of Ukraine?
reference_answer: Exxon Mobil announced in early 2022 that it would discontinue operations on the Sakhalin-1 project and exit the venture, recording about $3.4 billion of after-tax charges.

turns: Which company agreed in 2022 to buy another large industrial real estate owner?
reference_answer: Prologis agreed on June 11, 2022 to acquire Duke Realty in a stock-for-stock deal valued at about $25.5 billion.

turns: How does UnitedHealth calculate its medical care ratio?
reference_answer: UnitedHealth's medical care ratio (MCR) is medical costs divided by premium revenue.

turns: How does Bank of America measure the deposits that exceed insurance limits?
reference_answer: Bank of America's estimated uninsured deposits reflect amounts disclosed in its regulatory reports, adjusted to exclude related accrued interest and intercompany deposit balances.

turns: What an titrust ruling did Alphabet face in 2024, and what remedies could follow?
reference_answer: In August 2024 the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia ruled that Google violated antitrust laws relating to Search and Search advertising. A separate proceeding would decide remedies, which could include changes to products, services and business models, including structural remedies.

turns: How does the July 2025 tax law change the clean energy credits NextEra relies on?
reference_answer: The OBBBA, signed on July 4, 2025, speeds up the phase-out of the Inflation Reduction Act's clean energy tax credits: wind and solar facilities must be placed in service by December 31, 2027, among other requirements, to qualify for the technology-neutral PTCs and ITCs.

turns: How much was Prologis expected to pay for Duke Realty?
reference_answer: Prologis agreed on June 11, 2022 to acquire Duke Realty in a stock-for-stock transaction at a fixed exchange ratio, with an estimated acquisition price of about $25.5 billion.

turns: How did the war in Ukraine affect Linde's 2022 operating profit?
reference_answer: Linde's reported operating profit rose in 2022 as higher pricing, productivity and lower depreciation more than offset charges from the Russia-Ukraine conflict and the effects of inflation and currency.

turns: How did UnitedHealth describe the Change Healthcare cyberattack in its FY2024 10-K?
What did it cost them that year?
reference_answer: In its FY2024 10-K MD&A, UnitedHealth says that on February 21, 2024 it found cybercrime threat actors had gained access to some Change Healthcare IT systems. For the year ended December 31, 2024 it incurred $2.2 billion of direct response costs (including the costs of interest-free loans to care providers, higher medical care spending while some care management was suspended, network restoration and notifying affected people), and Optum Insight had estimated business disruption impacts of $867 million, mostly lost revenue. Medical costs from the temporary suspension of care management activities were about $640 million. It provided more than $9 billion of interest-free loans to care providers and estimated that about 190 million people were affected.

turns: What did Microsoft's FY2025 10-K say about expanding its datacenters for AI?
Does it say that spending will hurt its margins?
reference_answer: Yes. Microsoft says the investments it is making in cloud and AI infrastructure and devices will continue to increase its operating costs and may decrease its operating margins. In FY2025 the Microsoft Cloud gross margin percentage fell to 69%, driven by the impact of scaling its AI infrastructure, offset in part by efficiency gains in Azure.

turns: How did Coca-Cola and PepsiCo describe their operations in Russia in their FY2022 10-Ks?
reference_answer: Coca-Cola announced on March 8, 2022 that it was suspending its business in Russia because of the conflict between Russia and Ukraine, which also disrupted its business in Ukraine. PepsiCo suspended sales of Pepsi-Cola and certain other global beverage brands, its discretionary capital investments and its advertising and promotion in Russia, but kept offering its other products there. Russia was 5% of PepsiCo's consolidated net revenue in 2022 (4% in 2021) and 4% of its consolidated assets.

turns: How did Intel describe CHIPS Act funding in its FY2023 10-K compared with its FY2024 10-K?
reference_answer: FY2023: Intel expected to receive substantial grants from the US government under the CHIPS Act for planned new US fabs, and from the German government under the EU Chips Act for planned fabs in Germany, but said the amounts, timing and conditions of the funding were uncertain. FY2024: in November 2024 Intel entered into a direct funding agreement with the US Department of Commerce under the CHIPS Act, with detailed milestones it must reach to receive the funds (capital spending, facility completion, process technology, wafer production, insourcing Intel products, external foundry customers), limits on change-of-control transactions, sharing project returns above set thresholds with the government, and termination rights that could require repaying awards. Under the commercial CHIPS Act agreement it also agreed to forgo paying dividends for two years and to limits on dividends for the three years after.

turns: How did Pfizer describe revenue from its COVID-19 products in its FY2022 10-K?
And in FY2023?
reference_answer: In FY2023 Pfizer's total revenues fell $41.8 billion, or 42%, to $58.5 billion from $100.3 billion in 2022, mainly because of significant declines in revenues from Comirnaty and Paxlovid. That includes a $3.5 billion non-cash revenue reversal for Paxlovid in the fourth quarter of 2023, for the expected return of about 6.5 million treatment courses of EUA-labeled US government Paxlovid inventory. Excluding Comirnaty and Paxlovid, revenues grew 7% operationally.

turns: How did ExxonMobil's FY2022 10-K describe its exit from Russia?
How much did it cost?
reference_answer: After Russia's military action in Ukraine, ExxonMobil announced in early 2022 that it planned to discontinue operations on the Sakhalin-1 project and exit the venture. Its first-quarter 2022 results included after-tax charges of $3.4 billion, largely the impairment of its Sakhalin operations. On October 14, 2022 the Russian government unilaterally terminated its interests in Sakhalin by decree; fourth-quarter results include an after-tax benefit of $1.1 billion, largely from the effect of the expropriation on its obligations related to Sakhalin. About 150 million oil-equivalent barrels no longer qualified as proved reserves at year-end 2022.

turns: How did Delta describe the effect of fuel prices in its FY2022 10-K?
What does United Airlines say about passing higher fuel costs on to customers?
reference_answer: United says that, because the airline industry is highly competitive, it has historically had limited ability to raise its fares and fees enough to offset the full impact of fuel price increases, especially significant, rapid and sustained ones, and may not be able to in the future. Fare or fee increases may not last and may reduce demand for air travel. If fuel prices stay low for a long time, industry capacity and competition can rise and fares fall, and if prices then rise quickly, revenue may lag behind.

turns: What happened to Boeing's 737 program in 2024, according to its FY2024 10-K?
What stopped production later that year?
reference_answer: A strike: the International Association of Machinists and Aerospace Workers District 751 (IAM 751) work stoppage began on September 13, 2024 and paused production of the 737, 767, 777 and 777X and of commercial derivative aircraft for Defense, Space & Security (the KC-46A tanker and P-8A Poseidon). IAM 751 members ratified a new contract on November 4, 2024, ending the stoppage, and production of all programs resumed in December 2024. The stoppage significantly reduced deliveries in the second half of 2024, and the new contract and pay increases are weighing on Boeing's finances.

turns: How did General Motors describe the impact of tariffs in its FY2025 10-K?
What about Ford?
reference_answer: Ford's FY2025 10-K says its gross costs in 2025 from tariffs implemented or revised that year were about $3 billion, including the effect of tariff relief, and the net EBIT impact was about $2 billion after offsets. At December 31, 2025 it had recognized a $974 million receivable for tariffs paid but not yet refunded, and the timing of refunds is uncertain. Tariffs and supply-chain instability, including China's restrictions on exports of rare earth minerals and components, caused production disruptions and higher costs.

turns: Which Utilities companies discussed AI in their FY2025 risk factors?
reference_answer: From the word-checked cells: 27 of the 31 Utilities companies' FY2025 10-Ks have a risk-factor passage that names AI, including Ameren, American Electric Power, Constellation Energy, Dominion Energy, Duke Energy, Exelon, NextEra Energy, PG&E, Southern Company and Xcel Energy; 4 don't.

reference_answer: From the word-checked cells, mean polarity is close to -1 in every sector, so the differences are small: Information Technology (-1.11), Consumer Discretionary (-1.10) and Industrials (-1.07) are the most negative; Materials (-0.84) is the least negative.
